record.source: The sustained-improvement loop, rewritten for an instruction surface and a graded agent artifact rather than a codebase and a performance metric. The installed pstack package the file was read from carries no provenance of its own; its text is byte-identical to the file at this commit, checked by blob hash 582555e826675068ceaea08e6134a44ba0ea4511, so the pin is the revision read and not an approximation from a date.
record.kept: The loop's discipline: one change, one measurement, keep or revert, never stacking untested changes and never taking a win from inspection. The decision log with its row of fields, the stop predicate as a target plus a floor on attempts, the demand that a hypothesis names a mechanism, the plateau rule, and the reply's shape. The metric is fixed with its direction, the harness is proven sensitive and then frozen, and a baseline plus a green regression gate is recorded before any change.
record.rewritten: Three objects move to this repository's vocabulary. The metric becomes the score tuple read in order, because an instruction edit can gain a rule and lose the output shape. The harness becomes the eval harness, whose fixture, isolation root and bundle return are stated in `references/harness.md`. The regression gate is the case's own assertions plus the suite, which is what a broken behaviour fails. A hillclimb here is one climb over a series of paired batches rather than a baseline measured once, so drift is closed inside each batch.
record.added: The batch boundary: the previous state is re-measured as a control at the same run count, in one pass, or the comparison is cross-batch and proves nothing. Blinding of the grader comes from the pstack eval playbook, recorded as a citation, the workload patch is stated so the candidate's files are excluded and the two variables cannot interact, and the measurement reads the artifact rather than the child's report.
record.dropped: The code-specific workload dimensions (data size, history, state, concurrency), the architecture model taken from the `how` skill, the subagent's configured hillclimb model, the separate worktrees for parallel hypotheses as a worktree-management task, pushing past the first plateau as a stopping question, and the pull-request step, which this repository's delivery commit replaces.

record.source: One section of a 106-line skill, not the skill, hung under this repository's own title and arrangement. The installed package keeps `technical-writing` whole, because the three layers this file does not carry stay useful in the sandbox and nothing here competes for that name. The section is taken at the pin the clone is checked out at, `ae5650fe`, which is later than the pin on this source's other edge.
record.kept: The section and everything in it, in upstream's own words and order: the two questions, the four modes, the per-mode discipline, and the no-mixing rule.
record.rewritten: One character: the accent in `Diataxis`, which this repository's ASCII rule does not allow. Nothing else inside an upstream paragraph changes, so a bump diffs to insertions rather than rewrites.
record.added: The file's own title and opening line, the corpora table and the two corpora outside it, one paragraph after each of three modes, and the source line in this repository's citation form. Every addition sits between upstream paragraphs rather than inside one.
record.dropped: The three prose layers the skill opens with - Google developer style, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax - which are sentence-level rules for a different carrier; the section on varying rhythm; the instruction to propose abstract-metaphor offenders to `unslop`; and upstream's own `Source:` line, replaced by the citation form.

record.source: The upstream text was installed by hand into the agent config home and carried no provenance record, so the revision it was taken from is not recorded. The skill was specialized by hand against the upstream, so the differences from this pin are that specialization rather than drift. The lineage rests on the text: the skill shares eleven six-word runs with the pstack corpus, and it is the only skill in the tree that shares anything beyond an incidental phrase. The commits above are the first pin - the last upstream commit before this skill entered the tree at `c72df68b` - and not a recorded origin.
record.kept: The name, the `**Why:**` sentence, and the shape of a short principle with a pattern list. The name is kept because the judgement holds for any agentic work rather than for one surface, so it takes the bare `principle-` form under the project's suggested skill-naming scheme, `[<domain>-]principle-<judgement>`.
record.rewritten: Three clauses arrived that rebutted text the file no longer contained, addressed to whoever had made the edit rather than to a reader. The upstream text asserted that the context window is finite and non-renewable within a session, which is a capacity fact an agent cannot measure, and it instructed the reader to set turn budgets and account for mechanism costs, which name no counter and no price. Both are gone. In their place is a rule that names the reading which settles the question, and a rule that makes a pass countable. The two bullets upstream dropped, routing bulk to a subagent and keeping hot content inline, are restored, because both are executable and a skill that forbids nothing is not a guard.
record.added: `context.sh`, so measuring the room is a command rather than an intention. It reads the provider's own `usage.totalTokens` from `$PI_SESSION_FILE` and takes the denominator from the model catalog, so the number is measured rather than estimated. The skill is installed to `$AGENT_HOME/skills/principle-guard-the-context-window/`, which is the path `SKILL.md` names for `context.sh`.
record.dropped: A stopgap note that stated the file would be overwritten by a package bump. It was false, because no package ships this skill, and it was addressed to an editor rather than to the agent reading the skill.
